title: Privileged Likelihood Is Not Automatically Value: Three Checks for Token Credit in On-Policy Self-Distillation
abstract: arXiv:2608.09263v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: On-policy self-distillation aims to improve upon reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) by providing token-level scores derived from privileged information, such as reference solutions or critic feedback. These scores are treated as estimates of token-level action values, yet they answer a fundamentally different question: how the model's prediction changes when its input context is enriched, rather than how the expected outcome changes when a token is changed. We examine this gap along three dimensions: (i) whether the token-level score tracks task success; (ii) whether feedback generated from the same rollout causes the score to reflect agreement with its own description, and whether using feedback from other rollouts in the group mitigates this self-referential effect; and (iii) what behavior the resulting training objective actually reinforces. translated_title: 特权似然并非自动等价于价值：在线策略自蒸馏中令牌信用的三项检验
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.09263v2 公告类型：替换-交叉 摘要：在线策略自蒸馏旨在通过提供源自特权信息（如参考解答或批评者反馈）的令牌级分数，改进基于可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）。这些分数被视为令牌级行动价值的估计，但它们回答了一个根本不同的问题：当模型的输入上下文被丰富时，其预测如何变化，而非当某个令牌被改变时，预期结果如何变化。我们从三个维度审视这一差距：（i）令牌级分数是否追踪任务成功；（ii）从同一轨迹生成的反馈是否导致分数反映其自身描述的一致性，以及使用组内其他轨迹的反馈是否缓解这种自指效应；（iii）由此产生的训练目标实际强化了什么行为。在AIME 2025上的实验中，实现的分数区分了这些方面。
tldr: 本文提出三项检验，揭示在线策略自蒸馏中的特权似然分数并非自动代表令牌级价值，并验证其与任务成功和自指效应的差距。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes three checks showing that privileged likelihood scores in on-policy self-distillation do not automatically represent token-level values, and validates their gaps regarding task success and self-referential effects.
